The Story

Twenty years spent
closing the distance
between talent and opportunity.

Jeremy McNally has spent his career moving between rooms most people never get invited into — television studios, engineering floors, humanitarian outposts, UN panels — and building doors between them for everyone else.

He is a Florida-based entrepreneur, technologist, media executive, and nonprofit leader whose work sits at the intersection of visibility, systems, and service. Some days that looks like producing a national television segment. Others, it looks like handing out meals on a Saturday morning, or coaching an engineering team through a transformation that will outlast him.

The through-line is always the same — access. To people. To platforms. To capital, credibility, and the rooms where things get decided. Jeremy builds the bridges.

Based in Florida — working nationally & internationally

02 — Humanitarian Impact

Relief
Alliance

Co-founded with his son Aiden McNally, Relief Alliance exists for the people access hasn't reached yet. Its work is hands-on and unglamorous by design — homelessness outreach, food and clothing distribution, youth programs — built alongside longer pathways into education, work, and stability.

03 — Technology

A decade-plus
inside the systems
that run the room.

Before the media company and the nonprofit, there was the engineering floor. Jeremy's background spans software development, engineering leadership, Agile transformation, product delivery, automation, and applied AI — work he's carried through roles as a Software Engineer, Software Delivery Leader, Agile Coach, and Technical Dojo Coach.

At Edward Jones, his work in enterprise technology transformation, engineering coaching, and technical Dojos helped reshape how teams ship — including one initiative tied to more than $40 million in potential annual savings. Today, McNally Software carries that same discipline into consulting, AI enablement, automation, and rapid prototyping for founders and organizations building what's next.
